deep.reconstruction:
Context: cote 154 records Grothendieck's 1983-84 work on 'systèmes de pseudo-droites', i.e. arrangements of pseudolines and the combinatorial or cellular structures they induce. The previous page, dated 7.2.1984, sets up a cell complex K. Its old vertices have order 4 and its new vertices order 2, split into red (S'_K) and black (S''_K). Each face is a 4n-gon carrying edge signs ε_F(a). For each edge a there are face-to-face symmetries σ_a: Pol(F) → Pol(F'), which fix the 'grande arête' containing a and swap red and black vertices. This page is an earlier, and then abandoned, attempt at the same construction; it is struck through by two long pencil diagonals.

The aim is to subdivide K by adding vertices of index 2 in a canonical way, edge by edge over closed edges ā rather than face by face. The face-by-face version is crossed out.

Step a) On each closed edge ā, add the points of ā ∩ L, where L is the auxiliary curve system; these are the 'red points'. The result is the topological segment-graph a' = (a, (a ∩ S(K)) ∪ (a ∩ L)).

NB: there is at least one red point in the interior of a. Hence every sub-edge α of a' has at least one red endpoint, i.e. an endpoint that is not an endpoint of a. Exactly two sub-edges, the two extreme ones, have one non-red endpoint. On those two, no further vertex is added, with an inserted exception that is illegible.

On the other sub-edges, orange vertices are added:
- b) if both endpoints are non-critical (not on vertices of L), add one vertex, the midpoint;
- c) for an 'ordinary' edge, on either side of each critical point s ∈ S of order v(s), place v(s)/2 red points.

The page breaks off at this point.

The two sketches illustrate the rule. The left one is a yellow edge with red crosses (critical or old vertices, one labelled s) and red ticks (inserted points), with a cluster of ticks near the left end. The right one is a corner with a red cross and a single tick.

Purpose: to manufacture a 'regular' subdivided complex whose faces are 4n-gons with a red/black alternation and reflection-like symmetries. This gives a combinatorial normal form for the cell structure attached to a pseudoline system. The next page reformulates the same data intrinsically: critical points C_K with weights ν(s), and 'arcs of transition' of amplitude 2ν(s) centred at critical points.
errors: Not an error so much as an abandoned draft: the page is struck through and stops mid-sentence. The rule is incomplete: the exceptional case on the extreme sub-edges is illegible, and the treatment of c) breaks off.
Placing v(s)/2 points requires v(s) to be even. This is consistent with orders 2 and 4 elsewhere but is not stated here.

The claim that 'exactly two' sub-edges lack a red endpoint is only right when a has at least two interior red points. With exactly one interior red point, both sub-edges are extreme and the description degenerates; the case is not addressed.

ideas.what: Canonical edge-wise subdivision of a cell complex induced by an auxiliary curve system L: insert intersection points, then midpoints, then v(s)/2 points on either side of each critical vertex.
ideas.modern_name: Barycentric-type / regular subdivision of a cell complex; refinement of a CW structure adapted to an arrangement

ideas.what: Red/black (two-colouring) of order-2 vertices so that the faces become 4n-gons with reflection symmetries swapping the colours (from the surrounding pages).
ideas.modern_name: Flag/chamber-type structures, regular maps, reflection-group-like combinatorics of pseudoline arrangements
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses combinatorial maps and tame topology in general; unsure about pseudolines specifically

deep.surprise_reason: This is a crossed-out technical draft of a subdivision recipe, superseded on the neighbouring pages. It is routine combinatorics, interesting only as part of Grothendieck's unpublished pseudoline project.

'de point et d'autre des pts critiques' should read 'de part et d'autre des pts critiques'.
Date reads '2.1.84' in the image. The previous page is dated 7.2.1984, so this may be a misdating for 2.2.84, or the earlier draft.
The whole page is struck through by two diagonal pencil lines (abandoned draft), which the transcription does not note.
'il y a au moins un élément de a∩L' rather than 'NB [?] il y a': the '[?]' after NB is a crossed-out word.
